meta.title: GenAI at work — judgment — v4
meta.tagline: Study design blind; the units as extracted, categorised by the coder; the abstract's claims against their units. No numbers.
meta.description: The judgment workflow of the validation: (a) the study design and the screening criteria from the PDF alone; (b) the tasks, arms, outcomes, subgroups and horizons as the extraction listed them, each confirmed and categorised by the coder without seeing the model's category; (c) the abstract's sentences against the units they were matched to. Two coders per paper, independently. Taxonomy schema b5ed1ca67c; codebook in labeling/codebook.md.

fields.name: screen_ai_treatment
fields.label: Screening 1: AI as the treatment
fields.help: whether a generative AI tool is used while the measured work is produced, compared with the same work done without it (not met when the AI is used only before the measurement as a tutor, feedback tool or practice aid, when both arms use AI, when AI is only the researchers' method, or when it is evaluated on its own with no humans using it)

options.label: True
options.help: the criterion is met

options.label: False
options.help: clearly not met

options.label: Unclear
options.help: the paper does not let you decide; say why in study_notes

fields.name: screen_work_outcome
fields.label: Screening 2: a work outcome
fields.help: whether an outcome is the output of a work task, or of a task built to emulate one, judged on time, quantity, quality or accuracy (not met: grades and test scores, puzzles that stand for no job, how people worked rather than what they produced, a recipient's health or experience, well-being, attitudes, trust or perceptions alone)

options.label: True
options.help: the criterion is met

options.label: False
options.help: clearly not met

options.label: Unclear
options.help: the paper does not let you decide; say why in study_notes

fields.name: screen_design
fields.label: Screening 4: an experimental or quasi-experimental design
fields.help: whether the paper compares work done with the AI against work done without it by design: an RCT, a lab or field experiment, a natural or quasi-experiment, a single group before and after (not met: surveys, qualitative or case studies, reviews, theory, descriptive studies, a protocol without results)

options.label: True
options.help: the criterion is met

options.label: False
options.help: clearly not met

options.label: Unclear
options.help: the paper does not let you decide; say why in study_notes

fields.name: scale
fields.label: Scale
fields.help: the level at which the study examines AI's effects, by the primary unit of analysis and the level at which outcomes and conclusions are analysed, not by sample size or setting: a large sample of individual workers is micro; meso only when organisational outcomes are directly examined; macro only when aggregate labour-market or economic outcomes are studied; with several levels, the primary level of the empirical analysis

options.label: Micro
options.help: effects on individuals or small teams: worker productivity, behaviour, skills, task performance, also when the participants work within firms or across several organisations

options.label: Meso
options.help: effects on organisations, firms, workplaces or organisational structures: firm-level productivity, staffing, workflows, organisational performance

options.label: Macro
options.help: effects on labour markets, industries, regions or entire economies: aggregate employment, wages, occupational demand, economy-wide productivity

fields.name: research_design
fields.label: Research design
fields.help: the study's overall empirical design, by how AI exposure is assigned and how the study is organised, for the paper's main with-versus-without-AI comparison; a paper whose tasks differ in design takes the main comparison's, the others noted in task_notes; the estimator goes in identification_strategy

options.label: Lab RCT
options.help: participants randomly assigned to AI conditions in a controlled, in-person setting

options.label: Online RCT
options.help: participants randomly assigned in an online experiment or web-based setting

options.label: Field RCT
options.help: participants randomly assigned in a real workplace or market

options.label: Natural experiment
options.help: AI exposure arises from an external event or plausibly exogenous variation outside the researchers' control: a launch, a rollout, a policy

options.label: Observational
options.help: naturally occurring AI use or exposure analysed without experimental assignment and without an exogenous event; identification_strategy says how the comparison is made

options.label: Descriptive
options.help: describes AI use or outcomes without a treatment or exposure comparison

fields.name: identification_strategy
fields.label: Identification strategy
fields.help: the primary method used to identify or estimate the causal effect of AI exposure in the main comparison: the actual estimation method, not a broad label such as natural experiment; a specific strategy over generic regression adjustment

options.label: Random assignment
options.help: causal effects identified through randomized treatment assignment

options.label: Difference in differences
options.help: changes in outcomes between treated and comparison groups before and after AI exposure, staggered adoption designs included

options.label: Regression discontinuity
options.help: effects identified at a treatment-assignment threshold

options.label: Instrumental variable
options.help: an instrument that shifts AI exposure but is assumed not to affect outcomes directly

options.label: Interrupted time series
options.help: changes in outcome levels or trends after the AI's introduction, from repeated observations over time

options.label: Matching
options.help: comparable treated and untreated groups constructed on observed characteristics

options.label: Regression adjustment
options.help: statistical controls for observed confounders without a more specific identification strategy

options.label: Pre/post
options.help: outcomes before and after AI adoption without an untreated comparison group

options.label: None
options.help: no causal identification strategy is implemented

fields.name: experimental_design
fields.label: Experimental design
fields.help: whether the same people did the work with and without AI or different people did

options.label: Within person
options.help: the same people do the task with and without the AI

options.label: Across person
options.help: different people in the arms

options.label: Not applicable
options.help: no with-versus-without contrast at the person level

fields.name: unit_of_analysis
fields.label: Unit of analysis
fields.help: the unit the main estimates are computed on

fields.name: data_source
fields.label: Data source
fields.help: the data actually analysed, all that apply; not how participants were recruited or how data were collected: MTurk, Prolific and similar platforms used only for recruitment are neither online_freelancing_data nor online_platform_data

options.label: experimental data
options.help: data generated through a researcher-designed experiment or intervention

options.label: job postings
options.help: job advertisements or vacancy data

options.label: worker - household survey
options.help: survey data from workers, individuals or households, online surveys outside experiments included

options.label: firm survey
options.help: survey data from firms or employers

options.label: public admin data
options.help: government or public administrative records, e.g. Statistics Denmark

options.label: private admin data
options.help: internal firm or private administrative records, e.g. ADP payroll, HR or hiring records

options.label: AI usage data
options.help: observed AI usage or interaction data, e.g. the Anthropic Economic Index, Google ATLAS

options.label: online CVs
options.help: online professional profiles or employment histories, e.g. Revelio, LinkedIn

options.label: online platform data
options.help: observed activity or records from digital platforms, e.g. GitHub

options.label: online freelancing data
options.help: online freelance labour markets: freelancers, contracts, earnings or platform activity, e.g. Upwork, Fiverr

fields.name: period_start_year
fields.label: Data period start, year
fields.help: the year the data begin, as the paper states it

fields.name: period_start_month
fields.label: Data period start, month
fields.help: the month (1-12) the data begin, when the paper gives it; null otherwise

fields.name: period_end_year
fields.label: Data period end, year
fields.help: the year the data end, as the paper states it

fields.name: period_end_month
fields.label: Data period end, month
fields.help: the month (1-12) the data end, when the paper gives it; null otherwise

fields.name: sample_size
fields.label: Sample size
fields.help: the analysed number of human participants in the comparison that establishes the AI effect (the with-versus-without-AI design research_design describes), across its tasks; not a survey, descriptive dataset or pilot in the same paper; with several qualifying studies, the largest; people, never observations, tasks or firms (give those in study_notes); -1 if not stated

fields.name: preregistered
fields.label: Preregistered
fields.help: whether the study was preregistered (a registry, an analysis plan) as the paper states it

options.label: not stated
options.help: the paper does not say

fields.name: incentivized
fields.label: Performance incentives
fields.help: whether participants' pay, grade or advancement depended on their performance in the task (performance pay, a bonus, a graded assignment), not merely on taking part; if unclear, default to not_stated

options.label: not stated
options.help: the paper does not say

fields.name: vendor_affiliated
fields.label: Vendor affiliated
fields.help: whether an author is affiliated with, or the study was funded or run by, the provider of the AI tool studied (the firm that makes or sells it); read from the title page and the funding note by the coder, which the model does not see

options.label: not stated
options.help: the paper does not say

fields.name: focus_topic
fields.label: Focus topic
fields.help: the one topic the paper's stated research question speaks to first; the quote is where the paper states its question

options.label: Inequality
options.help: Findings are about inequality effects of AI.

options.label: Productivity
options.help: Findings are about productivity effects of AI.

options.label: Substitute complement
options.help: Findings relate to the substitutions of humans by AI and/or to AI and humans complementing each other.

options.label: Entry level
options.help: Findings speak to the debate on AI affecting entry-level jobs.

fields.name: focus_topic_secondary
fields.label: Focus topic (secondary)
fields.help: other topics the findings also speak to, each with its own quote; empty when there is none; never other beside a category that fits

options.label: Inequality
options.help: Findings are about inequality effects of AI.

options.label: Productivity
options.help: Findings are about productivity effects of AI.

options.label: Substitute complement
options.help: Findings relate to the substitutions of humans by AI and/or to AI and humans complementing each other.

options.label: Entry level
options.help: Findings speak to the debate on AI affecting entry-level jobs.

fields.name: focus_dimension
fields.label: Focus dimension
fields.help: whether the study focuses on workers (supply) or on employers' demand for labour (demand); both only when both are explicitly studied. Default to supply for worker-focused studies, including most AI productivity and collaboration experiments; never infer demand from productivity gains, economic outcomes or possible employment implications; demand only when employer labour demand is directly examined. Quote the paper's own statement of its question or findings, never a cited work

options.label: Demand
options.help: only studies explicitly examining employers' labour requirements: job postings, vacancies, recruitment, hiring patterns, skill demand, workforce expansion or reduction

options.label: Supply
options.help: any study about workers: their tasks, skills, behaviour, AI use, productivity, performance, wages or employment outcomes, including experiments with individuals, professionals or teams doing work tasks

fields.name: j_tasks
fields.label: Tasks
fields.help: the tasks the paper's participants performed, as the extraction listed them: the page tag opens the passage; confirm each and give its category

columns.name: task
columns.label: Task
columns.help: the task, then what it was in one sentence (numbers masked)

columns.name: category
columns.label: Category

options.label: Writing
options.help: Producing new prose text from scratch. E.g., drafting a cover letter, press release or essay.

options.label: Editing & Feedback
options.help: Improving existing text or work, or giving written feedback on it. E.g., revising a draft for clarity, giving peer feedback on an essay.

options.label: Summarizing & synthesis
options.help: Condensing or integrating given source material into a shorter account that stays faithful to the sources. E.g., summarizing a report, synthesizing findings from several papers.

options.label: Translation
options.help: Translating from one language into another while preserving the meaning.

options.label: Programming
options.help: Writing, modifying, debugging or testing code.

options.label: Data analysis
options.help: Processing and analyzing quantitative data to produce results, models or insights. E.g., running a regression, building a spreadsheet model.

options.label: Information search
options.help: Finding information from external sources to answer questions. E.g.,searching the web.

options.label: Problem solving & reasoning
options.help: Solving problems through reasoning. E.g., math problems, logic puzzles, exam questions.

options.label: Classification & detection
options.help: Assigning items to predefined categories. E.g., labelling X-rays as normal/abnormal, flagging fake news.

options.label: Evaluation & selection
options.help: Judging the quality of items or choosing among options, where no predefined category scheme exists. E.g., screening CVs, grading essays, picking an investment.

options.label: Forecasting
options.help: Predicting future outcomes or unknown quantities. E.g., predicting recidivism, forecasting sales.

options.label: Ideation
options.help: Generating new ideas or concepts. E.g., brainstorming product or business ideas.

options.label: Visual design
options.help: Creating visual artifacts. E.g., illustrations, UI mockups, slides.

options.label: Advising & recommending
options.help: Producing a recommendation tailored to a specific person's or organization's situation. E.g., a treatment plan, legal advice, a consulting recommendation.

options.label: Customer interaction
options.help: Real-time, conversational service with clients or customers. E.g., support chats.

options.label: Planning & scheduling
options.help: Producing a plan, schedule or allocation of resources over time. E.g., a project plan, event itinerary, shift schedule.

options.label: Persuasion & negotiation
options.help: Producing messages or bargaining behavior aimed at changing another party's beliefs, decisions or terms. E.g., writing a convincing message, negotiating a deal.

options.label: Physical & manual tasks
options.help: catch all for tasks where the core activity is bodily work or handling physical objects, materials or equipment. E.g., assembling components, operating machinery, providing hands-on patient care.

columns.help: the category the core activity falls in; type the paper's own term when none fits

columns.name: verdict
columns.label: Verdict
columns.help: blank or ok = a task as the paper has it; not_a_task = not a piece of work done by participants; split_or_merge = the paper has one where this lists two, or the reverse

fields.name: j_arms
fields.label: Arms
fields.help: the conditions of each task; the reference arm (marked) is the one the others are compared with

columns.name: arm
columns.label: Arm
columns.help: the condition, then what it got; the task it belongs to when the paper has several; the reference arm is marked

columns.name: category
columns.label: Category

options.label: reference arm · no AI, concurrent group
options.help: a concurrent group or condition doing the task without the AI, drawn from the same pool (randomized or assigned; design_type says which)

options.label: reference arm · no AI, the same units before
options.help: the same people or units before access: a pre-period, an own baseline, the not-yet-treated state of a rollout

options.label: reference arm · no AI, the same units after
options.help: the same people or units after the AI was taken away (a ban, an outage, the end of access): the time or group with the AI is the treatment arm, the one without it the reference arm, whatever the paper calls the treatment

options.label: reference arm · another, non-AI tool
options.help: the comparison condition got a non-AI aid instead: a search engine, documentation, templates, a checklist, non-generative software

options.label: reference arm · another AI
options.help: a different AI system or configuration is the comparison (an older model, no retrieval, a different prompt or interface, non-agentic); every arm uses AI

options.label: reference arm · expert benchmark
options.help: unassisted experts or incumbents whose performance is the reference for AI-assisted others: a different population, not an assigned condition

options.label: reference arm · the AI alone
options.help: the AI's own output with no human; recorded only when the paper's contrast is against it, with n_arm null

options.label: reference arm · external norm
options.help: a published norm, a historical rate or a market benchmark; no participants

options.label: reference arm · None
options.help: no comparison: a single arm, descriptive

options.label: treatment arm · Open-ended assistance
options.help: the human has open-ended access and uses it however they like; a general-purpose chatbot or agent is open_ended_assistance

options.label: treatment arm · AI review
options.help: The human produces the work and AI provides feedback.

options.label: treatment arm · AI advice
options.help: AI gives a recommendation like a prediction or a label but human makes decision. E.g. radiology image classification or algorithmic hiring

options.label: treatment arm · Human review
options.help: AI produces the work and the human reviews it.

options.label: treatment arm · AI-only
options.help: Full delegation with human limited to prompting, guiding and giving feedback.

columns.help: reference arm: what the comparison is against; treatment arm: how the AI took part in the work; type the paper's own term when none fits

columns.name: verdict
columns.label: Verdict
columns.help: blank or ok = a condition as the paper has it; not_an_arm = a subgroup, a period or a benchmark, not a condition; wrong = the description does not fit

fields.name: j_outcomes
fields.label: Outcomes
fields.help: the measures the tasks are scored on; give each its category (the kind of finding, its class in brackets). ◆ marks an index or composite that groups other listed measures: the index and its components are both listed, on purpose

columns.name: outcome
columns.label: Outcome
columns.help: the measure and its unit, then how it was measured; ◆ an index of other listed measures, and which; the task when the paper has several

columns.name: category
columns.label: Category

options.label: Time taken [performance]
options.help: time to complete a piece of work, or output per period: durations, counts per period, throughput, completion share

options.label: Output quality [performance]
options.help: the quality of the work: ratings on a scale, pass or acceptance rates, error and revision counts

options.label: Employment or hiring [labour market]
options.help: employment status, hiring, retention or attrition as the outcome

options.label: Wages or earnings [labour market]
options.help: pay, earnings or income as the outcome

options.label: Labour demand [labour market]
options.help: demand for workers or for a kind of work: vacancies, postings, hours demanded

options.label: Skill split [performance]
options.help: Lower- vs higher-skill effect

options.label: Task shift [behaviour]
options.help: Change in share/volume of a kind of work

options.label: Output diversity [performance]
options.help: Collective output diversity across people or items

options.label: Performance dispersion [performance]
options.help: the spread of performance across people: a slope by baseline skill, a variance, a correlation across tasks

options.label: Adoption or usage of the AI [behaviour]
options.help: adoption or usage of AI as the outcome

options.label: Secondary outcome [subjective]
options.help: well-being, attitudes, beliefs, trust

columns.help: the kind of finding the measure speaks to, with the class it implies [performance, behaviour, subjective, labour market]; type the paper's own term when none fits

columns.name: verdict
columns.label: Verdict
columns.help: blank or ok = a measure the paper reports for a task; duplicate = the same measure listed twice (an index and its components are not duplicates)

fields.name: j_subgroups
fields.label: Subgroups
fields.help: the subgroups the paper reports estimates for (the full sample is not listed)

columns.name: verdict
columns.label: Verdict
columns.help: blank = as in the paper; set only what is wrong

fields.name: j_horizons
fields.label: Horizons
fields.help: the horizons the paper reports estimates at (the post-treatment effect is not listed)

columns.name: verdict
columns.label: Verdict
columns.help: blank = as in the paper; set only what is wrong

fields.name: j_headlines
fields.label: Abstract sentences
fields.help: every sentence of the abstract, its numbers masked (#), with the unit the extraction matched it to spelled out: the task, the arm and its reference, the outcome, the sample and the horizon (v4: one field each, after the user's third look)

columns.name: sentence
columns.label: Sentence
columns.help: the sentence as the abstract has it (numbers masked); → no unit matched when the extraction tied it to no unit

columns.name: task
columns.label: Task
columns.help: the task the sentence was matched to

columns.name: arms
columns.label: Arm vs reference
columns.help: the treatment arm and the reference arm it is compared with

columns.name: subgroup
columns.label: Sample
columns.help: the subgroup the matched estimate is for, or the full sample

columns.name: horizon
columns.label: Horizon
columns.help: when the matched estimate is measured, or post-treatment

columns.name: verdict
columns.label: Verdict
columns.help: unit_right = the sentence is about this task, these arms, this outcome, sample and horizon; unit_wrong = about another; claim_without_unit = a result the paper reports that no listed unit covers; not_a_claim = background, method, implication

fields.name: notes
fields.label: Notes
fields.help: anything worth recording about this paper: a doubt, a rule you applied, a place to look at again

columns.name: text
columns.label: Text
columns.help: the passage verbatim; for a table its caption and rows as markdown

entries.label: Paper
entries.help: one per paper; the done button and the full-review flag
entries.title: {review_id}

fields.name: full_review
fields.label: Full review needed
fields.help: yes when what you saw makes the whole extraction of this paper doubtful; say why

stages.label: Study design
stages.help: From the PDF alone — nothing is prefilled and nothing is highlighted on this panel. Decide the three screening criteria first, then the design fields; a field the paper does not state stays empty. Use the marks tool (✎) to keep the passages you relied on; write doubts in Notes.

stages.label: Units
stages.help: The units as the extraction listed them, without categories and without numbers. Each row's page tag opens the passage it rests on. Confirm or reject each row (blank = as in the paper) and **give every task, arm and outcome its category** — a task's kind of work; the comparison a reference arm stands for or the part the AI played in a treatment arm; the kind of finding an outcome speaks to. ◆ marks an index that groups other listed outcomes. Add a row (＋) for a task, arm, outcome, subgroup or horizon the paper has and the list lacks.

stages.label: Headline
stages.help: Each sentence of the abstract (numbers masked) with the unit the extraction matched it to, one line each: the task, the arm and its reference, the outcome, the sample, the horizon. Say whether the sentence is about that unit. Then press done; set *Full review needed* when the paper's extraction as a whole looks doubtful, and say why.
